name: Fluorite
chronometers: Sm–Nd dating of mineralization; REE fluid tracer

matrix.title: Cube ↔ octahedron × modifier
matrix.subtitle: Fluorite runs from cubes to octahedra, with edges bevelled by the tetrahexahedron f{310} and corners by the hexoctahedron t{421} (the Weardale style).
matrix.note: The often-repeated rule 'cubes at low temperature, octahedra at high' is not supported here by a verified primary source, so the rows are descriptive. The Dana letter of the hexoctahedron is uncertain. Penetration twins on {111} are not modelled.

about: Fluorite's habit carries geochemistry: REE are taken up differently by {100} and {111} growth sectors (Bosze & Rakovan 2002). REE patterns trace hydrothermal fluids (Schwinn & Markl 2005), and Sm–Nd dates fluorite mineralization directly (Chesley et al. 1991).

habits.name: Bevelled cube
habits.text: f{310} or t{421} modifiers (columns f and t).

references.citation: Cheetham, A.K., Fender, B.E.F., Cooper, M.J. (1971). Defect structure of calcium fluoride containing excess anions I. Bragg scattering. Journal of Physics C 4, 3107–3121.

Bosze, S., Rakovan, J. (2002). Surface-structure-controlled sectoral zoning of the rare earth elements in fluorite from Long Lake, New York, and Bingham, New Mexico, USA. Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 66, 997–1009.
references.note: REE uptake differs between {100} and {111} sectors.

references.citation: Schwinn, G., Markl, G. (2005). REE systematics in hydrothermal fluorite. Chemical Geology 216, 225–248.
Chesley, J.T., Halliday, A.N., Scrivener, R.C. (1991). Samarium-neodymium direct dating of fluorite mineralization. Science 252, 949–951.
